newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends easier on RSS3 liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends easier on RSS3 liquidation.

text.p: Rubber futures closed marginally lower on Wednesday due to long liquidation by some market players, dealers said.

"It's a flat market. There was some liquidation by players in the market but almost nothing else was done in the other rubber brands. The whole thing was very, very quiet," a dealer for a foreign rubber broking house said.
Traders said market players were again sidelined after Tokyo rubber futures slid and amidst weak consumer sentiment.
"There was nothing by way of news to perk up trading today," another dealer said.

The volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached slightly under 1,800 tonnes, down sharply from the more than 7,800 tonnes traded yesterday. No trades were recorded for RSS1 rubber while only 200 tonnes were traded for TSR20 rubber.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 120.25-122.25 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.25 cents.
April RSS1 was indicated at 171.25-173.25 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.22) a kg from the previous 173.25 cents.
June TSR20 was seen at 168.50-170.50 Singapore cents (US$1.18-$1.20) a kg from 170.50 cents.
